title: Beef Wellington
summary: The ultimate showstopper for 5 people. Most work done day before - assembly day is manageable with timeline below. Serve with Orange Asparagus and optionally Savoury Crepes for wrapping.

steps.text: Sear beef fillet all over in hot pan with olive oil, 2 minutes per side until golden. Cool completely, brush with Dijon mustard, refrigerate.
Cook duxelles: Finely chop mushrooms, cook in batches over high heat with thyme and olive oil until all moisture evaporates and mixture is dry. Cool, refrigerate.
Make red wine sauce: Roast beef trimmings, add chopped shallots, deglaze with red wine, reduce by half. Add beef stock, simmer 1 hour, strain, refrigerate.
If using savoury crepes for wrapping, prepare them now (see Savoury Crepes recipe).
Roll out puff pastry to large rectangle. If using crepes, lay them overlapping on cling film.
Spread duxelles over pastry (or crepes if using), arrange Parma ham slices on top.
Place beef fillet in centre, use cling film to roll tightly into sausage shape. Chill 15 minutes.
Unwrap onto pastry (if using crepes, place crepe-wrapped beef onto pastry), wrap pastry around beef, sealing edges with egg wash. Score pastry decoratively.
Brush entire surface with remaining egg yolk. Refrigerate 30 minutes.
Bake at 200°C for 20-25 minutes until pastry is golden and internal temperature reaches 52-55°C for medium-rare.
Rest 15-20 minutes. Slice wellington into thick portions, serve with red wine sauce and Orange Asparagus.

tips: Temperature is critical - aim for 52-55°C internal for medium-rare (use meat thermometer). The single fillet cooks slightly faster than two separate ones. Traditional wellington uses savoury crepes as a moisture barrier between duxelles and pastry, but they're optional. Pair with full-bodied red: Cabernet Sauvignon, Bordeaux, or Syrah. For perfect slicing, use a very sharp knife and wipe between cuts.
